answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the knoll schedule in the yarrow ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the ridge checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 6 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 39 aliases thus means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest participants do not face at scale. That is 16 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
